The Protein Workbench

Load a structure, map every covalent and non-covalent contact, mutate a residue, relax it, and compare the interaction network and energetics before and after.

1  Structure
No structure loaded.
For a predicted model. pLDDT says whether a residue is placed well; only the PAE says whether two residues are placed well relative to each other. If Fetch is blocked, the files are at alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/<accession>.
Superposes the two, aligns their sequences, and reports how the interaction network differs rather than how the coordinates differ.
DCD, TRR or multi-frame GRO. Contacts then carry an occupancy rather than a yes or no.
Refines a placement that is roughly right; it cannot find one from nowhere.
No map loaded. With one, every residue and every contact is scored for whether there is density under it.
2  Contacts to detect
3  Mutation
The wild-type coordinates stay untouched; the mutant is built as a separate model you can download.
4  Energetics
Empirical force-field decomposition, not an alchemical free energy. See the Energetics tab for what each term means and what it cannot tell you.
5  Sampled free energy
Independent repeats set the uncertainty. Anything smaller than the error bar is not a result.
6  Crosslink geometry
Distances are measured as a path through solvent around the protein, not through it.
7  Network and scanning
8  Cavities and pockets
A cavity is space that cannot reach the solvent at all; a pocket is space that can, but is still enclosed on most sides.
9  Crystal environment
Generates the lattice neighbours and asks whether an interface in this file is biological or simply crystal packing.
10  Evidence
Reduces density, ensemble occupancy and prediction confidence to one support value per contact, then recomputes the network with it so you can see which conclusions depend on contacts that are not actually supported.
11  Water bridges
Needs waters: switch on "Keep waters" before loading. With several models or a trajectory, each bridge also gets an occupancy.
12  Elastic network
Predicted B-factors are the test of the model: if they do not track the deposited ones, the modes are not describing this structure.
13  Conservation
Conservation on its own says little. Crossed with contact strength and network centrality it says a good deal more.
14  Atomic force microscopy
A long comparison can run for hours: progress is saved as each fit finishes, and choosing the same files and settings again resumes it. Keep the computer awake.
Simulates what a tip of this size would trace over the molecule, and searches for the orientation that reproduces a measured topograph.
15  Structural dendrogram
Clusters structures by shape. It is a dendrogram of similarity, not a phylogeny, and the difference is not cosmetic.
16  Mechanics
Leave the two boxes empty to pull on the termini of the first chain. This is a ranking of susceptibility, not a force.
17  Electrostatics
A Poisson solution for the potential, and an estimate of how far each ionisable group is shifted from its value in free solution.
18  Glycans
Modelled sugars are used as they are; sequons with nothing modelled get a coarse exclusion volume, which is a proxy rather than a structure.
19  Design
Where a disulfide or a transglutaminase site could be placed, rather than where one already is. Both are geometric proposals and nothing more.
20  Binding hotspots
Ranks every interface residue by what alanine costs the interface, removes the ones not worth a mutant, then measures the leading candidates properly.
21  Batch
Runs one analysis across many files and ranks the result. The single-structure session is untouched.
22  Reproducibility
Records a hash of every input, the settings, and a digest of the results, so that a later session can be checked against this one.
Export
Each export also opens in the Export tab as copyable text, for environments that block saving files.
